newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico approves five remaining pension firms.
newsitem.headline: Mexico approves five remaining pension firms.

text.p: Mexico has approved the five remaining pension fund management firms, known in Spanish as Afores, including the only one with government participation, Afore XXI, a top pensions official said on Thursday.
"They are now all ready," Daniel Lederman, vice president of planning at the National Retirement Savings System Commission (Consar) told Reuters in an interview.

The approvals take to 17 the total number of pension fund management funds competing in the nascent industry, with total start-up capital said by Lederman to be around $640 million. The first 12 begun affiliating workers on February 3.
Among the five approved this week was Afore XX1, which Lederman said was made up of the Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS), Aseguradora Hidalgo and banking group IXE .
"They say that Bankers Trust is going to take some of the shares bought by IXE. IXE has 50 percent of this Afore. But we don't have formal news of this," he said.

The others approved were: Afore Capitaliza, owned by General Electric Capital Assurance Corp and G.E. Capital de Mexico; Afore Zurich, of Zurich Vida, the insurance company and private investors; an Afore formed by Grupo Financiero Promex Finamex and Grupo Financiero GBM Atlantico ; and Afore Confia, formed by Banca Confia and Principal Internacional Inc.
